messages.subject: Problem with 'dataProcess' and 'groupComparison' function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using 4.2.0 version of MSstats and I was following the youtube video and codes from the 2020 course.
(https://github.com/ZenBrayn/asms_2020_fall_workshop)

However, the 'dataProcess' function seem to have changed.
FIrst, the 'cutoffCensored' fucntion is no longer there. However, even when I run the dataProcess code with all default settings, the results are different. In the video course, it generates  'large list of 5 elements' while the new code generated 'Large list of 3 elements'.

I think this leads to the 'groupComparison' function also giving errors.
'Error in MSstatsContrastMatrix.matrix(contrast.matrix, groups) :
  Assertion on 'colnames of contrast matrix' failed: Must be equal to set {'Condition1','Condition2','Condition3','Condition4'}, but is {}."

I am wondering if you know what is going wrong?  I have used the exact files and codes from the github links above.

Best
Guanbin

messages.subject: Re: Problem with 'dataProcess' and 'groupComparison' function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

as indicated by the error message, MSstats requires a named contrast matrix. Column names of your matrix must be the same as your condition labels.
Please also see ?groupComparison and example("groupComparison", "MSstats"). The short course happened before the release of v4.0, but package documentation is up to date.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: Error in Spectronaut input format
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mateusz,

I figured out that there was a mistake calling the input data. Its working now, but I found that the spectronaut default stat and MSStats group comparison output is matching. I guess there are different model fitting in the background, but still the group comparison output looks little strange! there is only one protein that passed the adjusted p value, whereas around 400 proteins passed the ordinary p value. when the checked the spectronaut output, there are many that passed the adjusted p! Could you please check the codes. this is a directDIA output between WT and mutant and both of them treated/untreaetd (4 conditions). I have attached the group comparison output. here are codes I used:

spectronaut_imported <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(input,
                           annotation = NULL,
                           intensity = 'PeakArea',
                           filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
                           qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
                           useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
                           fewMeasurements="remove",
                           removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
                           summaryforMultipleRows=max,
                           use_log_file = FALSE)

spectronaut.proposed.normalized <- dataProcess(spectronaut_imported,
                                               normalization = "equalizeMedians",
                                               summaryMethod = "TMP",
                                               censoredInt = "0",
                                               MBimpute = FALSE,
                                               maxQuantileforCensored=0.999,
                                               use_log_file = FALSE)

comparison1<-matrix(c(-1,1,0,0),nrow=1)
comparison2<-matrix(c(0,0,-1,1),nrow=1)
comparison3<-rbind(comparison1,comparison2)

ELLU_proteome.comparisons1 <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison3,
                                             data = spectronaut.proposed.normalized,
                                             log_base = 2)

best,
Sudip

messages.subject: LOB/LOD calculation
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team,

I was using an old version of the MSstats package and after updating it to the most recent version, I realized that in the version 4.2.0 there are no longer the LOB/LOD estimation functions "nonlinear_quantlim" and "linear_quantlim".

Do you have now new alternative functions to do these estimations? If not, what are your recommandations for this type of LOB/LOD estimation using MSstats? Should I go back to using the older version of your package ?

Thank you in advance.

Best regards,
Tuvana Satar
